A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Event2vec by the same authors and retain identifiable methods and benchmarks. Text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. V2 ends after its references without an appendix; v3 includes readable Appendices A.1–A.9.

before.justification: Section 4 and Table 1 report original Event2vec classification results on DVS Gesture and ASL-DVS.

after.justification: V3 reports original classification results on three datasets, preprocessing and model timing measurements, embedding ablations, event-number experiments and visualization analyses.

M1.justification: V3 adds polarity-separated k-means aggregation and cluster-count weighting of spatial embeddings (Section 3.4), plus masked-coordinate pre-training with a decoder and reconstruction loss (Appendix A.5). It replaces gated linear attention with the Forgetting Transformer and revises pooling placement. Bidirectionality and the parametric spatial/convolutional temporal embeddings are retained.

E1.justification: V3 adds DVS-Lip, a 100-word lip-reading classification task, including masked-coordinate pre-training on its events. DVS Gesture and ASL-DVS remain. This extends the evaluated domain and task requirements beyond hand gestures and signed letters; the event-count sweeps are sampling changes within retained coverage.

E2.justification: For DVS Gesture, Table 1 adds FARSE-CNN and Event MAE and replaces the residual SNN cited to Fang et al. (2021) with Yao et al. (2023)'s attention SNN. Sparse GRU and both ASL-DVS comparators remain. New comparisons include DVS-Lip baselines, AEGNN timing and Araghi et al.'s voxel-grid sampling methods. Appendix A.7 specifies that SNN timing actually uses PLIF-Net as a substitute.

E3.justification: Reported settings change substantially: batch size falls from 128 to 64; 8 Gesture/512 ASL epochs become 64 epochs with dataset-specific repeats; Gesture sampling changes from 8192 to 4096 events and weight decay from 2 to 0. Model dimensions/depths and the stated learning-rate scaling formula also change. New timing protocols optimize batches/workers by method, and the training-data-usage metric is removed. The retained dataset splits are unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 adds spatial/temporal embedding ablations (Table 4), event-count sensitivity experiments measuring accuracy and computational performance (Figure 3), and comparisons with alternative sampling strategies (Figure 4). Figures 5–8 examine spatial smoothness, polarity relationships and event-level attention, including misplaced attention in lip-reading examples. V2 contains no corresponding empirical ablation or visualization suite.

E5.justification: V2 already averages repeated test-time sampling, using 18 Gesture and 16 ASL repetitions. V3 reports mean and standard deviation over 10 test runs for randomly sampled evaluations. It also specifies eight preprocessing measurements after two warm-up runs. Seeds remain fixed to zero; these disclosures do not establish repeated training across different seeds.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces Gesture's 96.01% accuracy and 3.22 MB model with 97.57±1.31% and 0.52 MB, and ASL's 99.80%/0.35 MB with 99.91±0.05%/0.27 MB. These results use revised configurations, preventing attribution to same-setting improvement. New DVS-Lip results are 70.62±1.55% for random events and 75.14% for cluster events. V3 also adds extensive timing, ablation and visualization findings and removes training-data-usage entries.

T1.justification: The locality condition and Taylor argument now perturb only spatial coordinates at fixed polarity, whereas v2 also perturbs polarity. Coordinate enumeration corrects ceiling division to floor division. Appendix A.5 introduces an inverse-fusion expression, but its printed Eq. (14), v_hat_m/rho minus v_t, does not invert Eq. (7) when rho differs from one. The bidirectional recurrence is largely retained and relocated.

C1.justification: The central event-to-vector representation and NLP-alignment contribution remain. V3 shifts the performance claims from training-data efficiency toward parameter efficiency, measured throughput and low-event robustness, with demonstrated lip-reading coverage. It drops v2's unqualified assertions about preserving all temporal resolution and eliminating preprocessing latency.

C2.justification: V3 adds substantive explanations of sampling information loss, the interaction between spatial inductive bias and temporal convolution, polarity relationships, and GPU kernel overhead. It also identifies lip-reading attention failures involving eyes and ears. These considerably expand v2's brief dataset-size explanation and prospective discussion of efficient deployment and generative applications.

D1.justification: Appendices A.3–A.8 add precision, gradient clipping, augmentation distributions, pre-training masks/decoder/loss, hardware, libraries, batch/worker settings and baseline implementation substitutions. The reproducibility statement gives more specific seed and artifact information, and the supplied repository address changes from a personal to a laboratory namespace. Conversely, v2's explicit replacement-sampling and padding-mask descriptions are no longer specified.

R1.justification: V3 substantially expands research positioning through a dedicated related-work section covering dense representations, point-based methods, neuromorphic hardware, GPU limitations and graph oversmoothing. It adds works supporting these comparisons and the Forgetting Transformer, while removing several earlier references, including ViT, gated linear attention and the coupon-collector sampling argument. These changes exceed citation-style or bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: Much of the retained prose is rewritten. The encoding analogy moves into the introduction, architecture moves from experiments into methods, and bidirectional equations and training details move into appendices. V3 introduces a dedicated related-work section and reproducibility statement and replaces the discussion with a reorganized conclusion.

P2.justification: V3 redesigns Figures 1–2, converts Algorithm 1 into inline mathematics, restructures Table 1 and adds timing, ablation and implementation tables plus several plots and visualizations. Figures 7–8 repeat some main-text embedding views while adding the second polarity. Layer normalization is omitted from the revised architecture drawing but retained in the text. The page template and figure/table placement also change substantially.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially addresses v2's limited empirical support for embedding design and efficiency through component ablations, measured timing benchmarks, lip-reading evaluation and detailed experimental protocols. Uncertainty reporting and attention-failure examples make the evidence easier to assess. The inconsistent inverse-fusion equation leaves part of the pre-training description unclear, and the disclosed SNN timing substitute limits that comparison, but these localized weaknesses do not outweigh the substantial gains in empirical support and reproducibility.
